todo_line: - [ ] 003 Implement the approved step plumbing and enable the two focused `custom_group_access_requests.feature` domain examples without changing their semantics or provenance.
outcome: The approved custom-group access-request feature runs at the domain layer and proves that an active KMC member can create the fixed ordinary Admin request message while a foreign or departed member creates no request message or group access.
scope: Implement Elixir domain-runner step plumbing for every currently missing step in `acceptance-tests/features/custom_group_access_requests.feature`, reusing compatible existing steps and the shared scenario context shape where they already exist.

Set up KMC, Alice and Dan as current club admins, Eve as an ordinary active member, and custom Board with Alice participating. Keep generated identities and emails scenario-local and use existing public Membership APIs with strong consistency.

For `Eve requests access to Board`, generate and remember one message ID, call accepted `Memba.Messaging.request_group_access/2` with only authenticated club/requester/target identities, and remember the result and resulting message for later assertions.

Prove the successful message is the ordinary root Admin conversation: subject and body identify Eve and Board, the body contains the club-hosted `/groups/:group_id/members/add/:person_id` URL, the Admin Group has write access, and projected email recipients are exactly Alice and Dan. This layer asserts accepted-for-send/projected recipients, not provider handoff.
Prove Eve remains outside Board after requesting and receives no new Board membership, Admin conversation access, or follow right from the request.

Implement both rejection rows in the scenario outline. Pat is a Nelson member with no KMC membership; Eve's KMC membership is ended before the attempt. Preserve each attempted message ID/result and prove the request is rejected, no message or Admin conversation/delivery is projected for that ID, and the actor gains no KMC custom/system-group participation or conversation access from the attempt.

Add a focused ExUnit wrapper for this feature, following the existing per-feature step-definition test pattern. It must execute the successful scenario and both expanded rejection examples and assert that the feature is selected by the domain runner.
Enable this feature by removing only its `@todo` tag. Retain `@iteration-066`, the feature/rule/scenario wording, examples, and all existing assertions unchanged.
scope_exclusions: Do not change application behavior, the accepted Membership resolver, `RequestGroupAccess`, message/event semantics, email delivery dispatch, or general web composition policy to make the scenarios pass.
Do not edit the browser journey or JavaScript browser steps; browser plumbing remains task 008.

Do not implement HTML email action rendering, the Request access LiveView affordance, placeholder copy/assertion changes, the targeted-add route, explicit Add, welcome behavior, or focus transitions; those remain tasks 004 through 007.

Do not edit `group_conversations.feature`, `journeys/custom_group_admission.feature`, any other feature semantics/tags, `plan.md`, `todo.md`, ADRs, project documentation, or planner-owned delivery artifacts.
Do not assert synchronous provider delivery or weaken the rejection/access assertions. Do not add request records, status, deduplication, or special test-only application APIs.
Do not run `dev check`, `dev check --quick`, `dev ci`, the browser acceptance suite, or another unscoped full-suite command in this packet.

references.facts: This is the approved domain contract. Keep `@iteration-066`, remove only `@todo`, and implement its successful scenario plus both rows of its rejection outline without rewriting the Gherkin.
Untagged non-journey scenarios run at the Elixir domain layer; `@todo` is removed only when that intended layer executes the examples.
The domain runner excludes `@journey` and `@todo`, expands outlines, merges shared context, and executes feature/rule backgrounds before scenario steps.
Use this per-feature ExUnit wrapper pattern to execute selected Cucumber scenarios and assert intended selection.

The existing `Alice and Dan are its club admins` step and helpers establish the context conventions: canonical KMC name, `:clubs`, `:people`, `:memberships`, and strong-consistency public Membership operations.

The existing `Pat belongs to Nelson Paddling Club but not KMC` step is reusable and demonstrates compatible club/person/membership context plus projected conversation, recipient, and access assertions.
Accepted task 002 supplies the composite request API and ordinary projected-message queries needed to drive and assert the feature without private storage access.

Accepted focused tests show the public input, fixed subject/body and ClubSite URL, exact Admin recipient/access shape, requester non-membership, and inactive/cross-club rejection behavior that the higher-level domain steps should express without duplicating forged-input permutations.
Use the server-owned KMC club summary and typed Board/Eve identities to form the expected absolute targeted-add URL contained in the stored body.

The acceptance contract requires one successful standard Admin request and rejection for someone who is not an active member of that club, while requesting grants no membership, follow, or conversation access.
A request is ordinary correspondence represented by MessageSent and fixed recipients; it has no request entity or lifecycle and does not add the requester to Board.
Recipient deliveries are fixed with the ordinary SendMessage decision, so domain assertions can inspect the existing projected deliveries.
Acceptance plumbing should exercise public Membership and Messaging APIs rather than query aggregates or context-owned storage directly.
Use deterministic strong-consistency/projection synchronization and avoid sleeps or unsupervised process setup.

constraints: Keep feature wording and semantics exact; only remove the feature-level `@todo` token while preserving `@iteration-066` provenance.
Treat the scenario outline as one approved rejection example with two required expanded executions: Pat in another club and departed Eve.
Use public context APIs and existing projected read APIs. Do not query event-store tables or Membership/Messaging Ecto schemas from the new step plumbing.
Use the accepted fixed subject `Access request: Board` and assert meaningful body facts and the exact ClubSite targeted-add URL; do not duplicate every lower-level command test.
Use the generated attempted message ID as the primary proof that rejected attempts persisted no message, access grant, follow, or deliveries; also retain the Gherkin's broader no-KMC-access outcome.
Do not dispatch pending email deliveries merely to prove recipient selection. The scenario says recipients, and accepted-for-send does not claim provider delivery.
Keep the new step module cohesive and avoid duplicating step expressions already registered by another module.
Do not use `Process.sleep/1`; all dispatches and assertions must use deterministic consistency options or existing barriers.
If the unchanged Gherkin cannot be implemented against the accepted public APIs, return the exact unresolved mismatch instead of changing scenario semantics or broadening into later obligations.
completion_evidence_required: Return every changed path and confirm that the only Gherkin change was removal of `@todo` while `@iteration-066`, all wording, both example rows, and provenance remained intact.
List the new/reused step expressions and identify which public Membership/Messaging APIs they exercise; report any deliberate reuse of existing registered steps.
Report the selected scenario names/count and show that the successful scenario plus both expanded rejection rows executed.

Summarize evidence for the ordinary Admin root conversation, fixed subject/body and targeted-add URL, exact Alice/Dan projected recipients, Eve remaining outside Board, and no request-granted access/follow.

Summarize evidence that both Pat and departed Eve are rejected and that each attempted message ID has no projected message, Admin conversation/access, follow, or delivery and grants no KMC group participation.
Record each focused validation command, exit status, and test/failure counts; list any unresolved issue without editing application behavior or later-task surfaces.

latest_review.summary: Task 002 was accepted with focused evidence that RequestGroupAccess creates the fixed ordinary Admin message and recipients, rejects inactive/cross-club actors, leaves the requester outside Board, and does not change feature files.

latest_worker_result.summary: The accepted implementation added the public application-layer request API and focused tests; its exact fixed content, URL, ordinary message events, rejection behavior, and projected recipient semantics are the implementation baseline for these domain steps.
